task.title: Turning it On For the First Time
task.shortdesc: Flipping the switch for the first time is the moment of truth for your build

context.p: You’ve planned and built your computer, and now it’s time to flip the switch! This is easily the most stressful and exciting part of the whole process, when you turn the power supply on, hit the power button on the case, and hope for the best.
If all has gone well the screen will come alive with the Power On Self-Test (POST) screen.

If instead, the computer just beeps at you, take note of the beeps. Those are an error message that can be used to diagnose the problem. Some motherboards have an LED display for error codes that can be helpful in troubleshooting.

If nothing happens the problem is most likely with the power supply: either the PSU itself is bad or produces insufficient wattage, the cabling is not fully connected, or you have forgotten to turn it on.
Anything short of shooting sparks is probably solvable eventually. In the worst-case scenario you’ve learned a lot, and Amazon, Newegg, and Microcenter will accept returns within 30 days.
If everything works you can close the case up, usually by sliding a panel into place and then tightening thumb screws on the rear. Congratulations!
